question.:question/problem:
The temperature $T(t),$ in degrees Celsius, of a body can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{dT}{dt}=-0.18(T-17)
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, measured in minutes. If the initial temperature of the body is ${48}^{∘}C,$ calculate the temperature of the body after $5$ minutes. Round your answer to the nearest integer.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We're told that the temperature of the body is modeled by the inhibited decay equation

$$
\frac{dT}{dt}=-0.18(T-17).
$$

First, we integrate our differential equation by separating the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dT}{T-17} & =-0.18\,dt \\ \int \frac{dT}{T-17} & =-\int 0.18\,\text{d}t \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|T-17| & =-0.18t+C\end{aligned}
$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited decay equation, we have $T-17>0$ for all $t>0.$
Next, we solve for $T(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T-17 & ={e}^{-0.18t+C} \\ T-17 & ={e}^{C}{e}^{-0.18t} \\ T-17 & =K{e}^{-0.18t} \\ T & =17+K{e}^{-0.18t}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $K={e}^{C}$ is a constant of integration. 

We're told that the initial temperature of the body was ${48}^{∘}C.$ So, we apply the initial condition $T(0)=48,$ and solve for $K:$

$$
\begin{aligned}48 & =17+K{e}^{0} \\ 48 & =17+K \\ K & =31\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to our initial value problem is

$$
T(t)=17+31{e}^{-0.18t}.
$$

Finally, the temperature of the body after $t=5$ minutes is

$$
T(5)=17+31{e}^{-0.18\cdot 5}≈{30}^{∘}\text{C},
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.

generation.domain: T(t)>ambient; positive rate; t>=0; observations strictly cooling

question.:question/problem:

$$
\frac{dT}{dt}=-0.1(T-66)
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, measured in minutes. If the initial temperature of the cake is ${259}^{∘}F,$ calculate the temperature of the cake after $3$ minutes. Round your answer to the nearest integer.
question.:question/worked-solution:

$$
\frac{dT}{dt}=-0.1(T-66).

$$

$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited decay equation, we have $T-66>0$ for all $t>0.$
Next, we solve for $T(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T-66 & ={e}^{-0.1t+C} \\ T-66 & ={e}^{C}{e}^{-0.1t} \\ T-66 & =K{e}^{-0.1t} \\ T & =66+K{e}^{-0.1t}\end{aligned}

$$

$$
T(t)=66+193{e}^{-0.1t}.
